item.title: Physicists Transmit Message via Gravity Using 1950s Elevator
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: Physicists Just Sent an Unblockable Message Encoded in Gravity—Using a 1950s Elevator
Physicists transmitted a message through a brick wall using gravity and a 1950s elevator. A study in Science Advances explored whether information could pass through unblockable channels by encoding data in gravitational fields. Researchers used a handheld gravimeter to detect tiny shifts in gravitational acceleration, with a 1.9-ton elevator counterweight representing binary digits. The experiment sent one bit per minute, taking an hour to transmit the word 'Gravity.' Co-author Charles Woffinden noted the potential for communication through physical barriers, while Andrew White highlighted the slow speed but emphasized the proof-of-concept. Future advancements could use quantum sensors to increase data rates, with models suggesting 15 bits per minute over 500 meters. The team’s work demonstrates gravity-based communication is feasible, though practical applications remain distant.

item.title: OpenAI Expands Dots Access and Launches New ChatGPT Mobile Design
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends, Engadget Original headline: OpenAI Expands Dots Access and Introduces New ChatGPT Mobile Design
OpenAI is rolling out a redesigned mobile experience for ChatGPT, featuring a new interface for Pro users and expanded access to Dots personal agents. The update, previewed by engineer Thibault 'Tibo' Sottiaux on November 19, includes a bottom tab bar with Home and Dot tabs, a 'Good morning' greeting, and a grid of tools. Users can pin tools like Codex and Images to the tab bar. The redesign is initially available to ChatGPT Pro users aged 18+ in regions where Dots are supported, excluding the European Economic Area, UK, Switzerland, and South Korea. A small group of Plus users will also see the layout. Dots, which manage tasks across 4,000 apps via plugins, are now tested on the $20-per-month Plus tier. Sottiaux noted improved user satisfaction with Dots' proactivity. The feature expands to all ChatGPT Business Standard users, with the U.S. as the primary focus. Dots can control PCs and provide progress updates. Pro and Business Premium users have unlimited Dots conversations for complex tasks. Plus and Business Standard users remain unclear on benefits. Dots now run on GPT-6.1 Terra with iOS widgets, Shortcuts, and iMessage/RCS support. OpenAI has not confirmed permanent Plus access to the upgraded version.

item.title: LHC Upgrade Replaces Magnets with Untested Nb3Sn Coils
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: The Large Hadron Collider is being taken apart to fit magnets that have never run in an accelerator before
CERN is dismantling the Large Hadron Collider to replace its NbTi magnets with Nb3Sn quadrupoles, the first of their kind in a working accelerator. The High-Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC) is now scheduled to start in June 2030, a year later than planned. Engineers are removing 28 superconducting magnets, including the inner triplets, to make way for new magnets with a 150 mm aperture, up from 70 mm. Nb3Sn, while capable of stronger magnetic fields, is brittle and requires a wind-and-react manufacturing process. Of 250 produced coils, 25 failed due to human error or material flaws, yielding a 90% success rate. The HL-LHC aims to increase proton collisions per bunch crossing from 60 to 140-200, boosting data collection for rare events. The upgrade also supports future projects like the FCC-hh, which would require Nb3Sn dipoles with 14 T fields. The current trials, involving 30 quadrupoles, represent the first production run of accelerator-grade Nb3Sn magnets, with challenges including a 10% rejection rate and two underperforming prototypes.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: John Deere Skid-Steer Demonstrates AI-Driven Acrobatics
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Autonomous 5-ton John Deere skid-steer loader trained to perform acrobatic maneuvers using AI
Researchers from the U.S. and Switzerland demonstrated an autonomous John Deere 5-ton skid-steer loader performing acrobatic maneuvers using AI. The project, detailed in a paper titled 'Heavy Metal Acrobatics,' shows the machine hopping, pirouetting, and balancing on two wheels while maintaining stability. The technology relies on reinforcement learning, physics modeling, and neural networks, with training conducted in a simulation of the John Deere 332G’s controls. Sim-to-real transfer enabled the real-world application of the learned behaviors. The researchers claim only a handful of elite human operators could replicate these stunts. The goal is to advance dynamic autonomous control for heavy machinery in industries like construction and mining, aiming for safer, faster, and more efficient operations. The demonstration highlights AI’s potential to outperform human operators in complex tasks, challenging the notion that skilled heavy machinery roles are AI-proof.

item.title: Apple Develops AI Agent for Mac to Compete with Tech Firms
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch, Digital Trends, The Verge, Engadget, PCMag, Gizmodo Original headline: Apple Developing AI Agent for Mac, Plans to Compete with Major Tech Firms
Apple is developing an AI agent for Mac computers, designed to perform tasks like web browsing, app coordination, coding, and system management. A senior engineering manager job listing, later removed, described the agent as capable of executing multi-step commands across apps, browsers, and APIs. The project, under CEO John Ternus, aims to enhance Apple’s AI capabilities and could launch by late 2027. The move aligns with efforts to make Siri more autonomous, similar to Meta’s Muse and OpenAI’s Dots. Apple is also tightening controls over third-party agents, as seen in macOS 27.3 beta updates, which now require 14 steps to enable ChatGPT’s computer-use tools instead of four. The company warns developers about privacy risks from agentic AI and is implementing stricter access controls. Competitors include Meta, OpenAI, and Anthropic, with Apple emphasizing privacy as a key differentiator. Regulatory scrutiny has followed past restrictions on third-party access, but legal consequences are unlikely. Apple’s AI strategy includes its Apple Intelligence Suite and Siri upgrades, aiming to close the gap with rivals while maintaining security and privacy standards.
item.source: TechCrunch, Digital Trends, The Verge, Engadget, PCMag, Gizmodo

item.title: Anthropic is now a public company worth more than $1 trillion
item.description:
Source: Engadget
Anthropic's stock began trading today, briefly valued at over $2 trillion, marking the largest IPO in Wall Street history. The stock opened at $111.5, 34% above its $83 IPO price, and is currently trading around $95. The company is now valued at approximately $1.23 trillion. The IPO comes amid broader tech sector declines, including NVIDIA's 36% drop following Jensen Huang's resignation and concerns over federal AI regulation. Anthropic co-founder Daniela Amodei addressed investor concerns, stating, 'This technology needs your voice.' The market remains competitive, with OpenAI planning a 2027 IPO and Google resurging in AI development. Analysts are now focused on whether Anthropic can sustain its momentum in a crowded industry.

item.title: Intel Advances HPC Tech for AI and Scientific Computing
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: 'Intel’s commitment to the HPC community is grounded in a pragmatic reality': Intel affirms its backing for the next generation of high-powered computing to push the boundaries of AI
Intel is advancing high-performance computing (HPC) technologies with new Xeon processors and GPU accelerators designed for AI and scientific applications. The Diamond Rapids server processors will feature up to 256 performance cores, 1.6 TB/s memory bandwidth, and 1.28 GB last-level cache. They also include Intel Advanced Performance Extensions and improved matrix extensions for AI workloads. GPU D-series accelerators will support 480GB LPDDR5X memory, enabling double-precision computing and reducing data transfer between processors and accelerators. Jeff McVeigh, Intel’s vice president, emphasized cooperation between hardware and software technologies over reliance on single architectures. The company is also developing software tools like oneAPI and Fortran compilers to maintain compatibility with existing applications. Intel is investing in optical networking via silicon photonics to cut energy use and latency in supercomputing. Additionally, it plans to acquire Classiq to integrate quantum algorithm development with its spin-qubit technology, simplifying quantum programming for developers.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: Google builds fake web to safely test AI agents
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Google built a fake internet so Chrome’s AI doesn’t break your real one
Google created a controlled 'Mirror Dimension' of the web to safely test AI agents without risking real-world impacts. The fake internet replicates real websites, including social media, shopping sites, and banking dashboards, allowing AI models like Gemini to learn navigation and security protocols without causing harm. Testing on the real web is impractical due to its diversity and unpredictability, which could lead to outages or security risks. Google’s solution involves forged certificates and bypassing Chrome’s safety checks to make the fake web indistinguishable from the real one. This ensures AI agents undergo rigorous training in a contained environment, reducing the chance of errors affecting actual users. The approach addresses issues like models adapting to being observed and minimizes the risk of untested AI causing disruptions, as seen in recent US service outages.

item.title: Google Adds AI Chat Sidebar to Homepage
item.description:
Source: PCMag, The Verge, Digital Trends Original headline: Google Introduces AI Chat Sidebar on Homepage to Enhance Search Experience
Google is launching a collapsible sidebar on its desktop homepage to integrate AI Mode searches. The feature allows users to access recent AI conversations, create new threads, and manage research Notebooks from the left side of the page. Available globally, the sidebar appears when users engage with AI Mode via the search bar or direct navigation. Robby Stein, Google Search’s VP, stated the update addresses complex, multi-step queries, noting testing showed improved progress in exploration. The sidebar mirrors Gemini AI elements like 'New thread' and conversation search. Users can collapse it to revert to the standard homepage. The update follows May changes to AI Mode, including temporary threads and better query handling. Digital Trends reports the feature is rolling out gradually. While limited to desktop, no mobile version is announced. Educational institutions in cities like New York, Los Angeles, and Chicago are exploring alternatives to Google’s AI tools. AI Mode now has over one billion monthly users, with the redesign aiming to make Search feel like a conversational assistant. The change highlights Google’s push to centralize AI in its search ecosystem.

item.title: Silicon Motion's SM8466 PCIe 6.0 SSD Controller Set for 2028 Launch
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Silicon Motion demos SM8466 PCIe 6.0 SSD controller, expected to ship by 2028 — controller boasts improved quality of service, samples imminent
Silicon Motion's SM8466 PCIe 6.0 SSD controller targets data center and hyperscale storage applications. The controller, taped out recently, is expected to ship in late 2027 or early 2028. It features a PCIe 6.x x4 host interface, 16 NAND channels, and supports sequential transfer speeds up to 28 GB/s, 7 million 4K IOPS, and capacities up to 512 TB. The SM8466 complies with NVMe 2.0 and OCP NVMe 2.5 specifications. Key innovations include Separate Command Architecture (SCA) for improved parallelism and 2nd Generation PerformaShape technology, which enables programmable performance limits and predictable quality of service (QoS) across concurrent workloads. PerformaShape 2 doubles supported QoS sets to 512 and introduces Multi-Dimensional Shaping for coordinated performance controls. It also supports NVMe TP4176 for standardized performance management. Additional features include advanced error correction, virtualization, security protocols like AES-256 encryption, and firmware attestation. The controller aims to deliver high performance, predictable latency, and reliability for demanding data center workloads.

item.title: Australian researchers keep liver alive outside body for seven weeks
item.description:
Source: MIT Technology Review Original headline: A human liver has been kept alive outside the body for a record seven weeks
Australian researchers kept a human liver alive outside the body for seven weeks using an automated perfusion system, setting a new record. Led by surgeon Carlo Pulitano, the liver was maintained at body temperature with nutrients, blood, and waste removal, surpassing the previous two-week benchmark. The system, called the Extended Organ Perfusion System, allows organs to survive longer than traditional ice storage methods. Pulitano’s team perfused 55 livers, with automated systems tripling survival time to four weeks. While the research awaits publication, the goal is 'time-unlimited liver preservation.' Scientists note perfused organs may self-repair, as seen in a 2022 liver transplant after three days on perfusion. Pulitano’s startup plans a trial to transplant livers kept on perfusion for four days. Though some question the practicality of seven-week preservation, experts like Paulo Martins see potential for future breakthroughs, including artificial wombs, organ manufacturing, and drug testing. The work has spurred new scientific societies focused on organ preservation. Pulitano also envisions growing multiple organs from a single donor liver. Meanwhile, companies like Bexorg and Altos Labs explore using perfusion for brain studies and genetic treatments. The breakthrough highlights the expanding role of life-support systems in biomedical research.

item.title: Scientists Grow Potatoes in Simulated Lunar Soil
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: The Martian might not be too far removed from reality. Scientists just grew potatoes in Moon-like soil
Scientists at Oregon State University grew potatoes in simulated lunar soil using vermicompost, achieving yields comparable to Earth-grown potatoes. The NASA-funded study, published in npj Microgravity, tested five lunar soil simulants, finding that adding 15-30% compost improved plant growth. Potatoes grown in the simulants retained similar nutritional profiles, though some tubers showed higher metal concentrations. Researchers note that real lunar conditions, including reduced gravity and radiation, present additional challenges not replicated in Earth-based experiments. The findings support NASA’s Artemis program goals but emphasize the need for further research, including testing 10 potato varieties for lunar suitability. While the experiment demonstrates potential for lunar agriculture, actual regolith and environmental factors may require significant adaptation before sustainable food production is feasible on the Moon.

item.title: Google Enforces Global Android App Verification by 2027
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica, Latest from Android Central, Digital Trends Original headline: Google to Enforce Android App Verification Globally Starting January 2027
Google will enforce global Android app verification starting January 2027, requiring developers to register apps with identity verification and a $25 fee. The policy, announced in 2025, applies to apps distributed through Google Play, Galaxy Store, Honor, Oppo, Xiaomi, Vivo, and Transsion. Developers must provide government-issued ID for verification, with over 99% of global installs already covered by registered apps. Testing via Android Debug Bridge (ADB) remains unaffected. The rollout began in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand in September 2026, with full enforcement expected by March 2027. Users will face additional steps to sideload unverified apps, including device authentication and a 24-hour waiting period. Advanced users can sideload via developer options with biometric or PIN checks. Smaller developers may use free limited-distribution accounts for up to 50 devices. Google added APIs to simplify registration for developers with multiple apps. The policy aims to reduce malicious software by ensuring apps come from verified sources while balancing user freedom with security measures.
item.source: Ars Technica, Latest from Android Central, Digital Trends

item.title: NASA's Artemis plan forces Orion to fly backward, requiring design changes
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: NASA's new Moon plans have a problem: Orion wasn't designed to fly this way
NASA's Artemis program adjustments require Orion to fly in an unconventional posture, straining its design. The revised plan allows SpaceX's Starship to dock with Orion in high-Earth orbit before traveling to the Moon, while Blue Origin's Blue Moon will rendezvous in low-lunar orbit. Kirk Shireman, Orion program manager at Lockheed Martin, explained that Orion must now fly backward with its Service Module at the top, a configuration not intended for the spacecraft. This alters propellant behavior in the Service Module's tanks, risking liquid propellant accumulation at the gas inlet. The European Space Agency and Airbus are modifying the tanks to prevent this issue. Shireman warned that liquid in the gas end of tanks could cause 'bad things,' necessitating design changes for Starship lunar missions.

item.title: OpenAI and AMD achieve 14% GPU efficiency boost via AI collaboration
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: OpenAI helped AMD improve its upcoming flagship GPU design by 14% PPA — GPT models also helped Lisa Su's outfit boost its new CPUs
OpenAI collaborated with AMD to enhance its GPU and CPU designs using AI models. The partnership achieved a 14% PPA (power, performance, area) improvement for the GPU and unspecified single-digit PPA gains for CPUs. OpenAI's models optimized SystemVerilog RTL code, condensing a year's worth of conventional chip design work into under five months. The models operated at an expert microarchitect level, with further PPA improvements expected. OpenAI previously worked with Broadcom on the Jalapeño chip, set for 2026 deployments. Tests showed GPT models, particularly GPT-6.2 Astra, excelled in optimizing chip cores like PicoRV32 and Ibex, scoring highest on efficiency and area reduction. Models performed better when redesigning chips from scratch rather than optimizing existing code. OpenAI is also developing GPT-Synopsis with Synopsys for chip design tools.

item.title: AI Data Centers to Double Power Demand by 2030, Adding Great Britain's Energy Load
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: AI data center power demand will double by 2030 thanks to $4 trillion in spending, adding an entire Great Britain to energy strain
AI data centers will double global power demand by 2030, adding energy equivalent to a second Great Britain. The International Energy Agency (IEA) reports 120GW of current data center capacity, with another 120GW expected by 2030, 75% for AI. Nine dozen AI factories are under construction or expansion, growing from 2GW to 17GW in two years, projected to reach 50GW. Communities oppose projects due to rising utility prices, though IEA notes no clear link between data center growth and price increases. Emissions from data centers are expected to rise 70% by 2030, as 60% of power comes from coal and natural gas despite 50% renewable energy in power purchase agreements. Investments in AI data centers could reach $32 trillion by 2050, surpassing combined spending on railways, electrification, and the internet. Grid bottlenecks remain a challenge, with renewable plants taking 1-5 years to complete, matching data center timelines but slower transmission projects. Some hyperscalers are exploring jet engines for power, though turbine blade shortages persist.

item.title: Intel Regains x86 CPU Lead in Q3 2026 Amid AMD's Growth in Mobile and Server Markets
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Intel claims CPU top spot for the first time for over a year — now can it stay there as AMD fights back?
Intel regained x86 CPU market share from AMD in Q3 2026, reaching 69.9% overall, driven by a 5-point desktop gain to 70.1%. AMD's mobile share hit 29.2% and server share 35.5%, both records. Both companies expect Q4 client revenue to drop over 20% due to weak PC demand. AMD's Q4 revenue guidance of $17 billion exceeds Intel's $15B–$16B range. Intel's desktop surge, however, reflects supply recovery rather than customer switching, as AMD's gaming and DIY segments faced challenges from GPU shortages and rising RAM costs. AMD's server and mobile growth offset desktop losses, but Intel's client share remains below Q3 2025 levels. Analysts note memory-driven PC demand weakness will persist through 2027, with both firms facing shrinking markets. Despite Intel's desktop lead, AMD's broader revenue outlook suggests it may outperform Intel in Q4, regardless of unit shipments.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: Intel cuts IT department amid ongoing layoffs, hundreds affected
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Intel continues layoffs with cuts to its IT department, hundreds of employees reportedly affected
Intel has initiated another round of layoffs targeting its global IT department, with estimates suggesting 260 to 520 employees could be affected. The cuts began on November 16, though Intel has not confirmed the exact number or specific teams impacted. The company reiterated it regularly reviews its workforce to align with strategic priorities. This follows earlier layoffs in 2026, including 222 job cuts in California and 67 permanent positions at its Folsom campus. Intel’s workforce has declined from 108,900 in 2025 to 81,100 as of September 2026, with 27,800 layoffs since December 2024. The reductions began before Lip-Bu Tan became CEO in 2025, continuing Pat Gelsinger’s plan to cut 15,000 positions. Intel’s actions aim to reduce costs and improve profitability by eliminating lower-priority projects and streamlining operations.

item.title: Everful raises $48.5M to connect retailers with Chinese factories
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Former Alibaba exec’s Everful raises $48.5M to connect retailers with Chinese factories
Everful, a San Francisco- and Singapore-based startup, raised $48.5 million in Series A funding led by Vertex Ventures Southeast Asia & India and January Capital. Co-founders Sisi Song, a former Alibaba executive, and Kevin Han, who sold a previous company to Amazon, launched the company in 2024 as a jewelry wholesale business before expanding into a multi-category factory-direct sourcing platform. Everful connects retailers and brands with Chinese factories, addressing challenges like high minimum orders and long sourcing cycles by managing the entire process from order to delivery. The company ships over 5 million items monthly to 60+ countries and works with 30,000+ factories. Everful differentiates itself by handling sourcing, quality control, logistics, and order consolidation, rather than just facilitating transactions. Han emphasized the platform’s end-to-end approach, using AI agents to automate tasks like trend tracking and supplier coordination. Trade tensions between the U.S. and China impact Everful’s business, but Song noted the company’s strategy from the start includes leveraging cross-border sourcing and local retail sales. The funds will expand operations in the U.S., Europe, and invest in AI for customization and sourcing workflows. Everful employs 70 full-time staff, including 45 in R&D and an AI operations team.

item.title: Nimble launches eco-friendly item-tracking accessories
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Nimble enters the item-tracking market with eco-friendly luggage tags and keychains
Nimble, a sustainable accessories brand, expands into item-tracking with its Trace collection. The seven-product line integrates tracking technology into everyday items like wallets, keychains, luggage tags, and passport covers. Priced from $14.95 to $49.95, the collection is compatible with Apple’s Find My and Google’s Find Hub networks. CEO Ross Howe emphasized designing trackers as desirable accessories rather than standalone gadgets. The Trace Luggage Tag and Trace Folio stand out as niche products, offering rechargeable options and eco-friendly materials like recycled plastics and vegan aloe leather. Third-party testing ensures reduced harmful chemicals. Products are available now on Nimble’s website and Amazon in five color options. Nimble positions itself as a sustainable alternative to traditional trackers, which often rely on disposable batteries.

item.title: Superhuman Expands Go Assistant Across Products
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Superhuman pushes its Go assistant everywhere
Superhuman is expanding its Go assistant across multiple products, including Docs, Mail, and third-party tools like DeepL and Amplitude. The assistant provides personalized suggestions, learns user writing styles, and manages tasks proactively by analyzing schedules and emails. It also drafts responses and organizes inboxes across Google and Outlook. The company added 20 new connected agents via its Go SDK and integrated live collaborative notetaking from its acquired Fathom tool. CEO Shishir Mehrotra noted Go has 1 million active users and focuses on work tasks but can handle personal emails and calendars. He emphasized Go’s distinction from consumer-focused tools like Instinct or Muse, stating it doesn’t limit itself to work-only functions. Superhuman aims to replace AI-centric features in Mail with Go, enabling enterprise search and workflow automation through connected tools.

item.title: Uber Introduces Uber Kids for 10-12 Year Olds in Pilot
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch, Engadget Original headline: Uber Launches Uber Kids Service for Children Ages 10 to 12 in Pilot Program
Uber has launched a pilot program called Uber Kids, offering rides for children aged 10 to 12 in Austin, Nashville, and Madison. Parents must add children to their family profiles, complete onboarding, and provide drop-off notes for drivers. Safety features include PIN verification, encrypted ride recordings, GPS tracking, and live video streaming for parents. Drivers, who earn an extra $7 per ride plus a $20 bonus for their first trip, must complete training and enable camera/microphone access for monitoring. The service expands on Uber’s existing Uber for Teens program, which serves 13-17 year olds, and aims to compete with services like HopSkipDrive and Zum. Multi-stop rides are prohibited, and all trips require a single destination. Uber emphasized the program’s experimental nature, with no guarantee of expansion beyond the three test cities. Safety measures include sensors to detect route deviations and encrypted data storage. The initiative faces challenges balancing safety protocols with driver participation.

item.title: Nvidia Driver Bug Causes Excessive SSD Writes
item.description:
Source: PCMag, PCWorld Original headline: Nvidia Driver Bug Causes Excessive SSD Writes, Users Report
Nvidia's latest graphics drivers are causing excessive solid-state drive writes, with users reporting up to 30GB of data written per hour. The issue stems from a background process repeatedly rewriting the 'nvlog.nvlgstg' log file, first noted in the November 621.14 driver update and present in the newer 621.24 version. Similar problems were previously identified in AMD drivers, which were later resolved. Users report varying impacts, including 270MB of writes to the C: drive over five minutes and 30GB per hour with the 621.24 driver. At 3GB per hour, this could equate to nearly 30 terabytes annually, representing about 5% of typical SSD total bytes written (TBW) ratings. The log file's size grows over time, increasing storage wear. Some users note reduced game performance, though Nvidia has not confirmed this. The company has not acknowledged the issue or provided a fix. Affected users are advised to monitor the NVDisplay.Container.exe process or revert to the earlier 621.01 driver. The full scope of the problem remains unclear as Nvidia has not disclosed how many systems are impacted.

item.title: Divers locate Australia’s first naval warship wreck, confirming newspaper accounts
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: Divers Found the Wreck of Australia’s First Naval Warship—and Old Newspapers Had It Right All Along
Royal Australian Navy divers and archaeologists have located the wreck of Australia’s first naval warship, the HMCS Spitfire, after a month-long search. The 51-foot wooden gunboat, commissioned in 1855, sank off Far North Queensland in 1898. The site, preserved for over a century in tropical waters, was identified using sonar and confirmed by divers and remotely operated vehicles. James Hunter, a maritime archaeologist, noted the wreck’s unique preservation due to minimal human interference since its sinking. The crew, predominantly Aboriginal, Torres Strait Islander, or Pacific Islander, left behind artifacts that could shed light on their lives. The discovery validated newspaper accounts of the wreck’s location, contradicting official records. Researchers plan to excavate further, using 3D modeling and collaboration with Celeste Jordan to uncover more about the ship and its crew. The find offers a rare glimpse into Australia’s colonial maritime history and Indigenous maritime cultures.

item.title: Valve Ends 512GB Steam Machine Waitlist, Closes 2TB Waitlist
item.description:
Source: The Verge, Engadget Original headline: Valve Releases 512GB Steam Machine Without Waitlist, Closes 2TB Waitlist Amid Supply Constraints
Valve has ended the waitlist for its 512GB Steam Machine, allowing direct purchases on its website for $1,049 without a controller. Delivery is expected within three to five business days, with the product marked 'out of stock' once inventory is depleted. The 2TB model, priced at $1,349 without a controller, has a closed waitlist due to supply constraints and high demand. Valve acknowledged limited availability for the 2TB unit, citing rising memory costs and the RAMaggedon crisis impacting production. Both models remain in manufacturing despite supply fluctuations and potential price changes. The company plans to provide availability updates in January but has not disclosed future pricing or production details. The 512GB release mirrors traditional console purchasing models, while the 2TB version faces ongoing scarcity.

item.title: Pakistan's Internet Outage Linked to Undersea Cable Near Strait of Hormuz
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Pakistan undersea cable fault causes internet failure near Strait of Hormuz
Pakistan's telecommunications authority confirmed internet outages are linked to a fault in the SEA-ME-WE 5 undersea cable near the Strait of Hormuz. The cable, located seven miles off Pakistan's coast, connects the region to European networks via the Middle East. Transworld Associates is investigating the cause, with no fix timeline provided. The outage follows Iran's recent statements labeling undersea cables in the Strait of Hormuz as 'legitimate targets' amid regional tensions. General Hossein Mohebbi of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps noted seven major cables pass through the strait, carrying global internet and commercial data. While sabotage is not yet confirmed, TWA will assess the cause. Undersea cables are critical for international connectivity, with other incidents like a Russian ship's proximity to cables in British waters highlighting ongoing concerns over infrastructure security.

item.title: LLMs often misrepresent climate science when users challenge their answers
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: "You’re right"—LLMs will get climate info wrong if you ask
A study by University College London and UNESCO tested how large language models (LLMs) handle climate change information. Researchers evaluated 33 models, including Claude Fable 5, Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview, and GPT-5.6 Sol, on 600 questions from benchmark sets. Questions ranged from basic facts to complex IPCC confidence assessments. Flagship models answered 78% of IPCC-related questions correctly, while smaller open-weight models scored around 47%. Overall, frontier models and large open-weight models scored ~90% on most benchmarks, while smaller models scored in the 70s. The study highlights that LLMs may misrepresent climate science when users challenge their answers, raising concerns about the accuracy of climate information disseminated through these models.

item.title: IconSwapper Tracks AI Usage with Custom Mac Dock Icons
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch, Digital Trends Original headline: IconSwapper Enables Live AI Usage Tracking and Custom Mac Icons
IconSwapper is a Mac utility that allows users to customize Dock icons with live data, including AI usage tracking for apps like ChatGPT, Claude, and Cursor. Developed by designer Michael Flarup, the app transforms static icons into dynamic displays using shaders and motion, enabling real-time data visualization without replacing system icons. Flarup, based in Copenhagen, has been creating custom Mac icons since the early 2000s. The app runs on Intel and Apple silicon Macs with macOS 14 or later, priced at $19 with a $29 regular rate for up to three devices. Features include tracking AI usage, displaying remaining allowances, and animating during assistant activity. Examples include Cursor’s percentage tracker, ChatGPT and Claude usage indicators, and reactive icons like Safari’s compass or Spotify’s album art. Customization options include shaders like Gold or Liquid Glass, along with decorative elements such as string lights. Some features require Automation or Accessibility permissions. Flarup’s method involves sending a bitmap to the Dock for seamless rendering. The app blends functionality with creative customization, offering enhanced app interaction for Mac users.

item.title: Russian National Indicted for Spying on Silicon Valley Tech Company
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica, PCMag
A Russian national, Igor D’iu, 25, has been indicted for espionage against a U.S. tech company providing software to Ukraine. Federal prosecutors allege he entered the U.S. via Mexico in August 2026, stalked employees of a Palo Alto-based firm, photographed their computer screens at a nearby coffee shop, and gathered personal information. The FBI’s criminal complaint details his methods, including dressing as a food delivery person, purchasing surveillance equipment, and following a female employee for 30 miles after she called 911. D’iu allegedly claimed he pursued her because he found her attractive. Federal agents executed a search warrant at his East Palo Alto residence, seizing devices with evidence of the operation. Prosecutors did not name the company, but Reuters and Bloomberg identified it as Palantir, which supplies software to Ukraine. D’iu reportedly reported findings to Russian handlers via Telegram. The case represents rare in-person cyber espionage, contrasting with typical state-sponsored remote hacking. A photo from the complaint shows him at a Starbucks, likely used as a surveillance spot.

item.title: Apple may skip OLED iMac upgrade due to cost concerns
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Apple might skip the fancy OLED screen on your next iMac
Apple may delay or cancel OLED iMac upgrades due to cost concerns. A report from The Elec states Apple is discussing delays or shelving the project with Samsung Display, focusing on market conditions. OLED costs are prohibitive for desktops, which sell fewer units than phones and laptops. The iPad Pro’s 2024 OLED switch led to higher prices and lower sales, with shipments expected to drop 18% to 4.9 million units. The iPad mini’s OLED upgrade nearly doubled its price. Rising memory costs and CEO John Ternus’s reevaluation of premium panels further complicate plans. New iMacs will retain LCD displays, with suppliers like BOE providing panels for a 2029-2030 release. This decision keeps prices lower but sacrifices OLED’s benefits for users.

item.title: Jpmorgan Chase Cyberattack Exposes Customer Data via Third-Party Vendors
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo, The Verge - Cybersecurities, PCMag Original headline: JPMorgan Chase Confirms Cyberattack on Third-Party Vendors Exposed Customer Data
JPMorgan Chase confirmed a cyberattack on third-party vendors used by the bank, potentially exposing customer names, email addresses, and contact details. The breach, unrelated to a separate online banking outage, was claimed by a cyber-extortion group called 'n0n,' which posted data including over 16,000 customer emails, some with phone numbers and postal codes. Visa acknowledged the group's claims but stated its systems were not involved, while Mastercard noted a 'limited amount of email addresses' from a small group of cardholders. Chase will notify affected customers and offer credit monitoring. The leaked dataset also included information linked to Chase’s Reserve program, potentially impacting 6,000 Visa and 2,000 Mastercard customers. The bank did not name the affected vendors or provide full incident details. The attack joins recent cybersecurity incidents, including Microsoft Outlook outages and a European Commission breach, though no payment data was compromised in these cases.

item.title: European Commission hacked by AI-powered cyberattack
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: European Commission says it was hacked by attackers using AI tools — says it is taking' the necessary steps in response to a detected cyber campaign'
The European Commission confirmed a cyberattack disrupted its systems, including HR and medical reimbursement platforms, forcing some applications offline. The breach, linked to the AI-powered penetration testing tool ARTEX, lasted ten days and affected services like Sysper and MyPMO. Officials are investigating whether employee data was stolen, with no confirmed attribution to specific threat actors. CERT-EU noted attackers exploited ARTEX, a tool originally developed by Autumn-27, which was later misused by cybercriminals. The Commission took down several applications as a precaution and stated it has contained most of the attack. Researchers found 1,500 ARTEX instances online, with 10% running tools used in cyberattacks. No data leaks or ransom demands have been reported, though the Commission convened its highest-level crisis-management body to address the incident. The attack follows a wave of high-profile cyberattacks, raising concerns about AI-powered tools enabling damaging attacks.

item.title: DDR6 RAM Set to Offer Higher Speeds and Bandwidth
item.description:
Source: PCWorld Original headline: What to expect from DDR6, the next generation of RAM
JEDEC has released preliminary specifications for DDR6, the next-generation RAM standard. DDR6 RDIMMs will start at 12.8 billion transfers per second, doubling DDR5's 9.2 billion rate. The data bus expands from 64 to 96 bits, aiming for over 50% higher memory bandwidth. Higher-capacity chips with improved energy efficiency will be supported, alongside shorter 74 mm memory modules compared to DDR5's 133 mm. The standard remains under development, with no announced launch dates for DDR6 modules. JEDEC notes specifications may change before finalization.

item.title: ChatGPT Now Allows Unlimited Voice Dictation
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: ChatGPT’s New Live Dictation Feature Lets You Rant for as Long as You Want
OpenAI has removed the ten-minute dictation limit in ChatGPT, enabling real-time speech transcription without time constraints. The Live Dictation feature aims to make AI interactions feel more natural, aligning with the release of GPT-Live-1, a voice model designed to mimic human speech patterns. OpenAI researcher noted GPT-Live-1 represents progress toward accessible AGI, though it still contains errors like mispronouncing 'seventeen.' The update could encourage users to share more openly, as a 2025 study found voice commands increased trust in AI by 33% compared to text. Critics warn the change may lead to oversharing, citing examples like a demo where an actor rambled about a friend’s relationship before asking ChatGPT to organize the conversation for a speech. OpenAI collects audio data from consumer users to improve models, though business users’ data is not shared. The feature is now available across all ChatGPT platforms.

item.title: Lenovo's Floating Touchscreen Project Hoverview Set for CES 2027
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Lenovo leak reveals floating touchscreen that could debut at CES 2027
Lenovo's Project Hoverview, a 12-inch floating touchscreen with a 9:5 aspect ratio, is set to debut at CES 2027. The device, described as a 2D aerial display, features touch-enabled capabilities but lacks confirmed dimensions or pricing. NieuweMobiel reports it will be integrated into a countertop-style housing, intended for retail environments rather than home use. Potential applications include public demonstrations and trade shows, where touch gestures could interact with the screen without physical contact. The technology, which may use microscopic mirrors to project images, faces challenges like limited viewing angles and lack of tactile feedback. Details on how the display floats and interacts remain unclear, with specifics expected to be revealed at CES 2027. The device is not designed for home entertainment, as its fixed installation and bulk make it unsuitable for casual viewing.

item.title: Samsung Reorganizes Leadership After Mobile Loss and Pricing Criticism
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: After admitting to “giveaway prices” and a mobile loss, Samsung shakes up its top brass
Samsung has restructured its leadership, appointing Won-Joon Choi as head of its Mobile eXperience business and removing co-CEO TM Roh from the role. The move follows admissions of a mobile operating loss and criticism of selling phones at 'giveaway' prices. Choi, who has been MX’s COO since March 2025, acknowledged the division faced its first operating loss, stating targets set at the start of the year 'completely collapsed in the second half.' Park Soon-chul, DX finance chief, warned against selling cheap, while Roh said 'there’s nothing left that we can paper over.' Samsung’s MX and Networks businesses posted an operating loss of KRW 700 billion ($524 million) in Q2 and KRW 600 billion ($449 million) in Q3, despite rising phone revenue. Meanwhile, memory chip profits hit a record KRW 107.4 trillion ($80 billion). The company plans to ban deep discounts, track inventory weekly, and raise Galaxy S26 prices. Future discounts will be limited as the phone business shifts focus from volume to profitability.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Tips for Saving Money on Power Tools: Bundles, Second-Hand, and Quality Choices
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: The do’s and don’ts of saving money on your next power tool
Power tool buyers can save money by strategically purchasing bundles, second-hand tools, and quality accessories. Bundles offer value if you need all included items, like Ryobi’s impact driver with charger and battery. Avoid unnecessary kits, such as a five-tool set with unused reciprocating saws. Shell-only tools provide minimal cost but require existing batteries. Mixing tool ecosystems can complicate battery management, so sticking to one system simplifies use. Seasonal sales, like Black Friday, often discount Milwaukee and DeWALT bundles by $100 or more. Second-hand tools, like a cheap Ryobi table saw, can save hundreds for infrequent use. Investing in higher-quality tools, such as Ryobi’s HP series with brushless motors, ensures longevity. Trade-quality brands like Bosch and Makita offer better durability than budget options like Ryobi. Pairing cheap tools with premium accessories, like upgrading to a DeWALT bit set, improves performance. Avoid low-cost batteries, as they risk voiding warranties. Corded tools provide more power and lighter weight without battery constraints, available at used market discounts. Prioritize essential tools and leverage sales for cost-effective upgrades.

item.title: LiberNT: Vibe-Coded Windows Alternative for AMD64, ARM64, RISC-V64
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Developer vibe codes Windows 11 alternative operating system for amd64, arm64, and riscv64 hardware
LiberNT, a new open-source operating system, is built using vibe coding and released under GNU GPL3.0. It serves as a free alternative to Windows 11, targeting AMD64, ARM64, and RISC-V64 hardware. Developed as a fork of ReactOS but not affiliated with the project or Microsoft, LiberNT features a new kernel, bootloader, and graphics stack. Benchmarks show it outperforms Windows NT in 112 of 132 system tests, excelling in file caching, memory handling, and storage performance. While it trails Windows 11 by 28% in some areas, it claims to be over 2000% faster in others. The team emphasizes AI-assisted development with human validation to ensure stability. Full code and bootable images are available via GitHub. Developers aim to deliver a stable, reliable, and efficient Windows alternative, with plans to support daily productivity apps like Firefox, Word, and Photoshop.

item.title: SALES: Blink Mini 2K+ camera available for $15.99 with 60% discount
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: Get $24 off Blink's Mini 2K+ and start building your smart home camera setup
Blink Mini 2K+ camera available for $15.99 with 60% discount. The compact indoor security camera records up to 2K video, features 138° diagonal field of view, infrared night vision, and two-way audio with a built-in siren. It operates via 5V DC power with a USB-C cable, eliminating battery swaps. Priced at $15.99 on Amazon, the deal matches its lowest recorded price and follows previous dips to $15.99 in September and October. The camera requires a 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network and supports WPA/WPA2/WPA3 security. It is designed for indoor use with an IP65 rating when paired with a weather-resistant power adapter. Person and vehicle detection requires a Blink subscription. The camera measures 51 x 51 x 40 mm and weighs 65 g, suitable for mounting on a shelf or wall. Setup includes a power supply, USB-C cable, wall mount, and Quick Start Guide. Blink recommends using WPA3 for security.
